key_insight: LLMPopSim shows that AI agent simulations can reproduce some community-level health behavior patterns, but accuracy varies by outcome and place.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers test public health interventions on synthetic populations before real-world deployment, while highlighting the need for careful calibration.
method: Built geographically grounded AI agent populations using U.S. Census and CDC data.
Tested the framework on colorectal cancer screening and mammography.
Evaluated transfer from Hawaii 2018 training data to held-out 2022 cohorts in Hawaii and New York State.
evidence_signal: Across four state-outcome evaluations, mean absolute error was 3.5 to 15.0 percentage points, with ZCTA-level correlations of 0.26 to 0.69.
watch_item: Performance was weaker in lower-prevalence communities and showed calibration and subgroup-fidelity challenges, so results should not be treated as directly reliable for decision-making.
paper_title: Evaluating agentic simulation for local public health estimation
